source: NCERT Class XI, Performing Arts & Cultural Heritage of India, Ch. 2 (Indian Classical Music: Hindustani and Carnatic).

sections.heading: 1. Foundations of Indian Classical Music
points: Indian classical music is based on the **raga** (melodic framework) and **tala** (rhythmic cycle).
Its roots lie in the **Samaveda**; the treatise **Natyashastra** and later **Sangita Ratnakara (Sharngadeva)** codified it.
Two main systems: **Hindustani (North India)** and **Carnatic (South India)** — they diverged around the 13th–14th centuries.

sections.heading: 2. Hindustani Music (North)
points: Influenced by **Persian/Central Asian** traditions; **Amir Khusrau** is credited with innovations (and the sitar/tabla, qawwali).
Organised into **gharanas** (schools/lineages).
Forms: **Dhrupad** (oldest, austere), **Khayal** (most popular), **Thumri, Tarana, Ghazal**.
Ragas are linked to **times of day/seasons**; the **that** system classifies ragas.
Instruments: sitar, sarod, santoor, tabla, sarangi, bansuri.

sections.heading: 3. Carnatic Music (South)
points: More **composition-based** and devotional; strong continuity of ancient tradition.
The **Trinity of Carnatic music**: **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri**.
**Purandara Dasa** = 'Father/Pitamaha of Carnatic music' (systematised teaching).
Main form: the **kriti/kirtana**; the raga system uses **72 melakarta (parent) ragas**.
Instruments: veena, mridangam, ghatam, violin, flute.

sections.heading: 4. Hindustani vs Carnatic — Contrast
points: Hindustani = more **improvisation (alap)**, gharana-based, Persian influence; Carnatic = more **composition-centric**, unified.
Both use raga + tala; differ in style, repertoire and instruments.
Both are living oral traditions transmitted **guru–shishya (teacher–disciple)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Raga = melody; tala = rhythm; roots in Samaveda.
Hindustani = North (gharanas; Dhrupad, Khayal, Thumri); Amir Khusrau's innovations.
Carnatic Trinity = Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri.
Purandara Dasa = Pitamaha/Father of Carnatic music; 72 melakarta ragas.
Hindustani = improvisation; Carnatic = composition (kriti)-based.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Carnatic Trinity = Tyagaraja, Dikshitar, Syama Sastri**.
**Purandara Dasa** = father of Carnatic music (systematised teaching).
**Dhrupad** is the oldest Hindustani form; **Khayal** the most popular.
**Hindustani = North (Persian influence)**; **Carnatic = South**.
